unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who: (1) has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months; (2) has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (referencing § 825.801 for special hours of service requirements for airline flight crew employees); and (3) is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) regarding employees who work outside the U.S.).
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three requirements must be met: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.

unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided that the conditions of paragraph (b) are met.
unit_attributes.scope_text: Provided that the conditions specified in paragraph (b) are met.

unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months (which need not be consecutive), subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.

unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq., covered service obligation; or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (e.g., for purposes of the employee furthering his or her education or for childrearing purposes).
unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where an employee has a break in service of more than seven years, and either the break was occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation or a written agreement concerning rehire exists.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation, OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (e.g., for education or childrearing purposes).

unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer.
unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, where the break in service or absence is due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.

unit_attributes.statement: Section 825.110 does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA.
unit_attributes.scope_text: Regarding entitlements under section 825.110 in connection with USERRA-covered service.

unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment.
unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.).

unit_attributes.statement: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.
unit_attributes.scope_text: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.modality_quote: Nothing in this section prevents employers from

unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.
unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
